You're prepping backlog-refinement notes for a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann) FED Lead, for Jira ticket SFCC-315 "Cart Drawer PWA Kit Component". Read-only research — you are not writing to Jira or Confluence.

SHARED GROUND TRUTH (cite, don't re-derive):
- Today is 2026-09-03. Real Sprint 4 runs 2026-08-24–2026-09-07 (active now); Sprint 5 runs 2026-09-07–2026-09-21. The repo's .docs/memory/sprintScope.md is CONFIRMED STALE — judge this ticket on its own Jira status/fields.
- Figma 04.7 Component Inventory (Confluence page 400195591, re-checked live today, unchanged since 2026-08-10): the generic "Drawer" component's row literally reads "Designs Empty" across every column, status "Incomplete". This is a real, current design blocker, not a stale artifact.
- IMPORTANT cross-story pattern: two OTHER tickets in this same refinement round — SFCC-801 (global/country-currency-selector) and SFCC-831 (global/country-language-mismatch) — both explicitly describe themselves as "a right-anchored drawer panel using the shared drawer shell" / "a right-anchored slide-in drawer." All three tickets (this one plus those two) appear to depend on the same generic Drawer shell whose Figma entry is "Incomplete". Worth surfacing as one shared blocker affecting three stories, not three separate blockers — and worth asking whether one shared PWA Kit Drawer shell component should be built once rather than three times.
- ALSO CHECK: SFCC-736 "pdp/drawer" is a different, already-merged ticket (PR #67, "Ready for QA") that built PDP slide-out tabs. Fetch it (jira_get_issue) and check whether its underlying shell implementation is generic/reusable (a real drawer/slide-out primitive) or PDP-specific plumbing that doesn't generalize — this could substantially de-risk this ticket and its two siblings if reusable.
- Cart PRD (.docs/prd/cart.md) §1 (CAI-001): "Opens as an overlay on Add to Bag CTA or bag icon click" — confirm this ticket is that mini-cart overlay (vs. the full cart page, which is a separate surface).
- New Zimmermann components live at overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/ — check overrides/app/components/ for any existing drawer-shaped component (note: overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/ exists as the site-navigation hamburger drawer, Tier 2 Global Shell — that is a DIFFERENT thing from a generic content drawer/slide-out shell; don't conflate them, but do check whether drawer-menu's underlying primitive is reusable).

DO THIS:
1. Fetch the full ticket: jira_get_issue(issue_key='SFCC-315', fields='summary,description,status,issuelinks,comment,attachment,parent', comment_limit=20).
2. Fetch SFCC-736 (jira_get_issue) for the reusable-shell check above.
3. Check overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/ briefly (Read/Glob, don't need to read every file) for its underlying mechanism.
4. Apply the seven-point sizing lens: (1) any FE impact? (2) is the requirement clear enough to size? (3) which surfaces does it touch? (4) design/Figma dependencies? (5) API/backend dependencies? (6) pure FE, shared FE/BE, or needs architecture input? (7) size now, or need clarification first?
5. Read for the four standing axes: behaviour, desktop/mobile, a11y (focus trap, Escape-to-close, return focus on close), data — flag anything genuinely unclear.
6. Design dependency — this one's likely a hard no given the tracker; state it plainly.
7. Altitude: BAs own component-decomposition questions, devs own atomic/build questions.

OUTPUT, in this exact shape:
- One-line plain-language summary
- Seven lens answers
- Four axes, flagging what's unclear
- Design status + source (be explicit about the "Designs Empty" finding)
- The shared-drawer-shell cross-story flag (SFCC-801/SFCC-831 also need this) and the SFCC-736/drawer-menu reusability check
- Specific questions to raise, each tagged with who should answer it
- One-line readiness call

Be concrete, don't editorialize past what the data supports, and say plainly what you couldn't check.

This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. 1	# PRD – Cart & Inventory
2	
3	*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Cart & Inventory" and "Order Management". Last updated: 2026-06-19.*
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Mini-Cart (CAI-001 – CAI-005)
8	
9	- Opens as an overlay on Add to Bag CTA or bag icon click (CAI-001)
10	- Per line item: product image, name, colour, price (was/now if on sale), size, quantity, item total (CAI-001, CAI-006)
11	- Actions per line item: Move to Wishlist, Remove (CAI-004)
12	- **Move to Wishlist is authenticated-only at launch** — only logged-in customers can move a mini-cart item to wishlist; an unauthenticated user selecting Move to Wishlist is prompted to log in first (CAI-004). Guest wishlist capability is a logged enhancement, not in scope for go-live — see Section 4.
13	- Subtotal (incl/excl tax per storefront) with Checkout CTA navigating to checkout entry (CAI-002), and View Bag link to full cart page (CAI-003)
14	- **"Recommended for You" carousel** beneath bag contents — recommendation engine platform TBC (SFCC Einstein vs Athos Commerce), see Open Items (CAI-005)
15	- No recommendations in checkout or order summary — mini-cart and cart only (CFD-021)
16	- International customers (as determined by selected shipping country): Checkout CTA redirects to Global-e checkout
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 2. Cart Page (CAI-006 – CAI-017)
21	
22	- Per line item: image, name, colour, size, price (was/now), quantity controls (increment/decrement — CAI-007), item total
23	- Actions per line item: Remove, Move to Wishlist (CAI-008)
24	- **Move to Wishlist is authenticated-only at launch** — only logged-in customers can move a cart item to wishlist; an unauthenticated user selecting Move to Wishlist is prompted to log in first (CAI-008). Guest wishlist capability is a logged enhancement, not in scope for go-live — see Section 4.
25	- Order summary: item count, subtotal (incl/excl tax per storefront), shipping (TBC at checkout), tax where applicable, grand total in local currency (CAI-009)
26	- Promo code field (CAI-011) and Checkout CTA (CAI-010)
27	- Empty cart message shown when cart is empty (CAI-012)
28	- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) per order — error displayed if exceeded (CAI-017)
29	- Price changes while item is in cart are automatically reflected; no customer notification required (CAI-016)
30	- Sale pricing (was/now) displayed consistently across mini-cart and cart page (CAI-013)
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 3. Cart Persistence (CAI-014 – CAI-015)
35	
36	- **Guest cart:** persisted for **30 days**
37	- **Logged-in cart:** persisted **indefinitely**
38	- **Cart merge on login:** if a guest adds items and then logs in during checkout, carts are merged (CFD-006)
39	- **Separate bag per storefront** — a customer's AU bag and US bag are independent (CRM-170)
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 4. Wishlist (CAI-018, CRM)
44	
45	- Wishlist requires authentication — guests attempting to save are redirected to login (CAI-018)
46	- **Size-level** wishlist; single global wishlist; one size per product
47	- 18-month inactivity cleanup
48	- Shareable via email
49	- Back-in-stock notifications from wishlist items
50	- Guest wishlist (with merge on login) is **out of scope for go-live** — captured in the enhancement log (CAI-018, ENH-039)
51	- **Wishlist hosting platform (SFCC vs Omneo) is being sized, not confirmed** — see Open Items (ENH-038/039). The Move-to-Wishlist login-prompt behaviour (CAI-004/008) is independent of where the wishlist is ultimately stored.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 5. Inventory Display (CAI-024 – CAI-031, OM-021 – OM-032)
56	
57	### Feeds
58	- Daily full inventory feed from NewStore via MuleSoft (CAI-019)
59	- Delta feed via MuleSoft every **15 minutes** (confirmed — CAI-020)
60	- All inventory calls routed through MuleSoft — never SFCC directly to NewStore (CAI-022)
61	- Mulesoft delivers a combined available-to-promise figure aggregating warehouse and eligible boutique stock per region; this aggregate drives browse-level availability states (Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock) (CAI-023). MuleSoft's ability to perform this aggregation is unconfirmed — see Open Items.
62	
63	### Buffer stock
64	- Configurable buffer threshold **per SKU per storefront** in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-024, CAI-025). Applied at SFCC level, not in the feed itself.
65	- Category-level fallback retained; SKU-level takes precedence; thresholds are **not additive**.
66	- Business users can set buffer stock via bulk upload (by category, colour, store view).
67	- **ADD TO BAG** shown when variant stock exceeds buffer threshold (CAI-026)
68	- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when stock is above zero but at or below buffer threshold; Add to Bag disabled and back-in-stock capture presented (CAI-027)
69	- **OUT OF STOCK** also shown when variant stock is fully depleted; same disabled state and back-in-stock capture (CAI-028)
70	- Low-stock indicator shown at size level — **no quantity number displayed**; not displayed in mini-cart or cart (CAI-030)
71	- Business users can suppress OOS products from PLP (CAI-031)
72	
73	### General availability vs. boutique stock
74	- General browsing uses a combined (buffered) stock figure
75	- Boutique inventory: real-time call to NewStore via MuleSoft, **no buffer applied**, only triggered when Find in Boutique flyout panel or BOPIS boutique selection screen is opened
76	
77	---
78	
79	## 6. Reservation (CAI-032 – CAI-036)
80	
81	- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart
82	- **Hard reservation** only at order placement
83	- Real-time inventory check via NewStore/MuleSoft when customer proceeds from cart → checkout entry; desired behaviour confirmed, but a new MuleSoft flow is required as none currently exists — see Open Items (CAI-034)
84	- If an item is OOS at checkout entry: Checkout CTA is disabled; customer must remove the item. No auto-removal (CAI-035/036)
85	- Cart notifies customer when an item becomes OOS while in cart (CAI-035)
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 7. Find in Boutique (CAI-037 – CAI-042)
90	
91	- Button shown on PDP for eligible products
92	- Opens as a flyout panel (CAI-037)
93	- On open: real-time call to NewStore via MuleSoft once a size has been selected (the call is per-size and refreshes when the customer selects a different size — CAI-038)
94	- No auto-refresh while the flyout panel is open
95	- Per-boutique availability for the currently selected size: **In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock** (CAI-039)
96	- **No buffer stock** applied to boutique inventory; true physical NewStore OMS stock levels are displayed (CAI-040)
97	- Boutique stock cached with a configurable TTL (set in Business Manager — CAI-042)
98	- Display a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size (CAI-041)
99	- *Open item: location-aware fallback (serve inventory from a nearby boutique based on user location) flagged as a potential post-launch enhancement (CAI-041, to discuss)*
100	
101	---
102	
103	## 8. Collect in Boutique / BOPIS (CAI-043 – CAI-045)
104	
105	*Scope: UK, AU, EU domestic storefronts only.*
106	
107	- Real-time call to NewStore OMS via MuleSoft when the customer selects Collect in Boutique, validating both store eligibility and stock availability for the selected item and size (CAI-043)
108	- On order placement, the order is submitted to NewStore OMS with the selected boutique as the fulfilment location; NewStore routes and assigns to boutique staff (CAI-044)
109	- Collect in Boutique availability responses cached on initial OMS call, refreshed on TTL expiry; TTL configurable in Business Manager (CAI-045)
110	
111	---
112	
113	## 9. Exclusive / VIP Products (CAI-046 – CAI-047, CRM-162 – CRM-164)
114	
115	- Exclusive/VIP items are **visible only to eligible customer groups**; customer group membership is managed via Omneo and configured in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-046)
116	- Ineligible customers cannot see these items in search or PLP (CAI-047)
117	- A **private marketing URL** grants access to exclusive VIC products without requiring login or customer group assignment at browse time — but purchase is still restricted to the eligible group (CRM-162)
118	- **VIC Exclusive tag** displayed on PLP tile and PDP for eligible customers
119	
120	---
121	
122	## 10. Back-in-Stock Notifications (OM-033 – OM-034)
123	
124	- Customer captures email on OOS product; the notify-me email and product details are submitted to **Emarsys** (CAI-029)
125	- Back-in-stock email sent to the first configurable-N customers on a FIFO basis when stock returns above buffer
126	- **No loyalty tier prioritisation** — strictly FIFO
127	- Guest capture timing is subject to the Omneo guest record creation open item (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")
128	
129	---
130	
131	## 11. No-Split Orders (CFD-033, CAI-033)
132	
133	- No order splitting — all items in an order are delivered to the same address
134	- Customer is informed post-purchase if items ship in multiple parcels (via Narvar)
135	
136	---
137	
138	## 12. Open Items
139	
140	- **CAI-005 — Recommendation engine for mini-cart carousel not confirmed.** The requirement text now reads "powered by SFCC Einstein (or Athos Commerce pending search platform decision)", but the row's open comment "Search / reccomendation engine not confirmed" persists and RJ adds "It is 99% likely we will move away from Athos". Treat platform (Einstein vs Athos Commerce) as undecided. **FLAG — cross-sheet contradiction:** Third_Party_Integrations (Search and Recommendations / Salesforce Einstein) states the system "will use Salesforce Einstein for all search, merchandising and product recommendation functionality across all storefronts," which contradicts CAI-005 treating the engine as unconfirmed. Do not silently resolve — confirm with Zimmermann which sheet is authoritative.
141	- **CAI-023 — MuleSoft warehouse + boutique aggregation feasibility.** IC: "We had a requirement that for a SKU/size to be considered 'in stock' then it would take into account an aggregated view of warehouse & boutique stock... Will Mulesoft be able to do this?" SFCC OOTB does not aggregate; aggregation capability pending confirmation.
142	- **CAI-034 — Real-time cart→checkout inventory check requires new MuleSoft flow.** "Currently the Mulesoft does not exists for this, and will require a new MuleSoft flow. Otherwise, we will just use inventory feed." Behaviour desired/confirmed, build dependency open.
143	- **CAI-041 — Location-aware boutique fallback.** RJ: "We need to consider the users location and we could potentially serve inventory from a nearby boutique." Potential post-launch enhancement.
144	- **CAI-037/039 — Find in Boutique design marked Phase 2.** Requirement Confirmed; designs not yet available for go-live timing.
145	- **ENH-038 / ENH-039 — SFCC-hosted wishlist being scoped (not confirmed).** Previously out of scope (wishlist to migrate to Omneo); both enhancements now flipped — ENH-038 (add OOS products to wishlist from PLP) Zimm response: *"ACN to size — wishlist in SFCC"*; ENH-039 (guest wishlist consolidating on login) Zimm response: *"ACN to size"* / *"To be sized"*. A SFCC-hosted wishlist for go-live is being sized but not confirmed. The Move-to-Wishlist behaviour (CAI-004/008) depends on whether the wishlist ultimately lives in SFCC vs Omneo (cf. ENH-040, which logs the SFCC→Omneo migration as a separate enhancement). Both still status "Under Review" — confirm hosting platform and go-live scope with Zimmermann before build.

1	import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
2	
3	// Figma pdp/drawer: Large = 50% of viewport width, Small = 25% — Tim confirmed (2026-08-27)
4	// to build Small to the named 25%, not the 27.9% actually measured in the current Figma frame;
5	// he is flagging that discrepancy to the design team separately.
6	const WIDTH_LARGE = '50%';
7	const WIDTH_SMALL = '25%';
8	
9	// Mobile deliberately leaves a strip of backdrop visible below the panel (SFCC-736 AC 9,
10	// PO-approved 2026-08-21 — "so a user can easily navigate out"). Figma measured ~78px;
11	// var(--zimm-scale-5xl) (80px) is the closest named-scale match, kept pending Tim's separate
12	// design/PO confirmation of the exact value.
13	const MOBILE_BOTTOM_GAP = 'var(--zimm-scale-5xl)';
14	
15	// Close-button inset, measured from the pdp/drawer header frames. Small and Mobile share the
16	// same measured inset (32px/40px) at every width; Large only switches to the wider 48px/64px
17	// inset at/above the tablet breakpoint — below it, `large`'s variant override doesn't apply and
18	// the compact baseStyle inset is used instead, which is also how the whole drawer collapses to
19	// the mobile treatment on a narrow viewport regardless of the chosen `size`.
20	const INSET_COMPACT = { top: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)' };
21	const INSET_LARGE = { top: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-4xl)' };
22	
23	export const ZimmDrawer = {
24	  parts: ['overlay', 'content', 'closeButton'],
25	  baseStyle: {
26	    // Explicit position/inset rather than relying on Chakra's own built-in `Drawer` overlay
27	    // styling — confirmed via inspection that it doesn't apply (renders `position: static`,
28	    // zero size) when the `<Drawer>` isn't given Chakra's own `size` prop, which this component
29	    // deliberately omits (see maxWidth note below). Owning it here avoids depending on that.
30	    overlay: {
31	      position: 'fixed',
32	      inset: 0,
33	      background: 'var(--zimm-color-opacity-50)',
34	      zIndex: 'overlay',
35	    },
36	    content: {
37	      width: '100%',
38	      // Matches `width` at every step below — Chakra's own `Drawer` theme defaults to
39	      // `size="xs"` (maxW 20rem) when no `size` prop is passed to `<Drawer>` (deliberate: its
40	      // fixed size scale has no 50%/25% steps), and that default `maxW` otherwise still caps
41	      // our own `width` override since we never reset it.
42	      maxWidth: '100%',
43	      bottom: MOBILE_BOTTOM_GAP,
44	      // Header stays fixed; only the content area (ZimmPdpDrawer's own `content` part) scrolls —
45	      // AC 10, "content area scrolls independently without the tab header scrolling".
46	      display: 'flex',
47	      flexDirection: 'column',
48	      overflow: 'hidden',
49	    },
50	    closeButton: INSET_COMPACT,
51	  },
52	  variants: {
53	    large: {
54	      content: {
55	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
56	          width: WIDTH_LARGE,
57	          maxWidth: WIDTH_LARGE,
58	          bottom: 0,
59	        },
60	      },
61	      closeButton: {
62	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: INSET_LARGE,
63	      },
64	    },
65	    small: {
66	      content: {
67	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
68	          width: WIDTH_SMALL,
69	          maxWidth: WIDTH_SMALL,
70	          bottom: 0,
71	        },
72	      },
73	    },
74	    // No override — the baseStyle above already is the mobile treatment.
75	    mobile: {},
76	  },
77	};

content.text:
## SFCC-315 Backlog Refinement Notes — "Cart Drawer PWA Kit Component"

**Summary:** This ticket asks for the reusable drawer *shell* for the mini-cart overlay (container, header states, open/close, responsive layout only — line-item content and a11y are explicitly deferred elsewhere) — and a generic drawer atom that structurally matches what it needs (`ZimmDrawer`) already shipped in this codebase via a sibling ticket, but neither ticket links to the other, so reuse is a strong inference, not a confirmed decision.

Ticket facts not in the brief: status "Tech design" (To Do), priority High, **assignee is Marcel Angelo Navarro (you)**, reporter Isabel Chaloner, labels `CAI-006`/`Custom`/`Squad-A`, parent epic SFCC-11 "Cart," created 2026-08-04, last updated 2026-09-01. Approved by Emma Kirwan (2026-09-01): *"this ticket is approved... any reference to copy is purely indicative... should be configurable or needs to be formally signed off."* No formal Jira `issuelinks` exist on SFCC-315 at all — the "dependency for" list (SFCC-270, 274, 316, 318, 404) is prose-only inside the description, not structured Jira links, and there is no link to SFCC-736 either.

### Seven-point sizing lens

1. **FE impact:** Yes, entirely FE — a React component build. No SFCC/BE logic is named in this ticket's own scope.
2. **Clear enough to size:** Partially. Scope boundaries are well-written (shell only; no a11y — "just a variation of the drawer component"; no line-item content). But I could not find an itemized Acceptance Criteria list in any field (`description`, or a full `fields=*all` fetch) — Emma's comment references "sign off of the acceptance criteria" but the only text present is the narrative description, so either ACs live somewhere I can't see or they're less granular than the sign-off comment implies. The bigger sizing swing is unresolved reuse: the description never names `ZimmDrawer` or SFCC-736.
3. **Surfaces touched:** Cart epic (SFCC-11), but the drawer is triggered from Header (bag icon) and PDP/PLP (Add to Bag) per PRD CAI-001 — both are cross-squad/Global-Shell-adjacent (`header/` is Tier 2, "Both Squads" per `protectedFiles.md`), though this ticket itself only builds the shell, not each trigger wiring.
4. **Design/Figma dependencies:** Yes, and layered — see Design status below, plus a separate, easy-to-miss third design source: the open/close **animation** spec lives on an external Vercel handover page, not Figma.
5. **API/backend dependencies:** Narrow but real — the shell needs at minimum basket state (empty vs. populated, for "header states"). No backend integration is being built here; the basket hooks already exist (Tier 1, `use-current-basket.ts`).
6. **Pure FE / shared / architecture:** Pure FE, but touches an existing architectural rule worth confirming explicitly: `components.md`'s container/presentational separation says a component under `overrides/app/components/` shouldn't call basket hooks itself — that belongs to a page/container. SFCC-315 calls itself "the container component for all other cart stories," which is ambiguous between "structural container" and "owns the data fetch."
7. **Size now or clarify first:** Lean toward one clarifying question first (ZimmDrawer reuse, below) — it swings effort substantially and determines whether the ticket's own a11y exemption is actually valid. A rough directional size is possible today; a confident one isn't yet.

### Four standing axes

- **Behaviour:** Unclear specifics. "Header states" (plural) isn't enumerated — the two attachments (Full Cart / Empty Cart) suggest at minimum empty-vs-populated, consistent with PRD CAI-012, but nothing confirms whether loading/error/OOS-in-cart states are in scope here or deferred to a child story.
- **Desktop/mobile:** "Responsive layout" is named but no specific breakpoint behaviour is given. If this reuses `ZimmDrawer`, it has three named size variants (`large` 50%, `small` 25%, mobile full-width-with-backdrop-strip) — SFCC-315 doesn't say which one the cart maps to.
- **A11y:** Explicitly out of scope in the ticket text, punted to "the drawer component." **This is conditionally true, not unconditionally true** — see the reuse-check below. If reuse is confirmed, focus trap/Escape/return-focus/body-scroll-lock are already handled (via Chakra's Drawer primitive, per `ZimmDrawer`'s own doc comment). If the team instead builds a bespoke drawer, this becomes a real, unscoped gap on a core commerce flow.
- **Data:** Needs at least basket-empty vs. has-items (+ count) for header state. Unclear whether this component receives that as props (container/presentational rule) or fetches it directly. Also worth confirming out of scope for *this* ticket: CAI-016 (price-change reflection) and CAI-035 (OOS-while-in-cart notification) touch this same drawer surface but read as child-story territory, not this shell.

### Design status

Per the given ground truth (Figma 04.7 Component Inventory, Confluence 400195591, re-checked live today): the generic **"Drawer" component row reads "Designs Empty" across every column, status "Incomplete."** Taken alone, that's a hard blocker for a ticket whose job is literally to build a drawer variation.

But ticket-level evidence complicates that reading, and I want to flag the contradiction rather than pick a side:
- SFCC-315 has two attached mockups (Full Cart / Empty Cart, Isabel Chaloner, 2026-08-25), a "Cart Designs" Figma link, and a "UI Design Kit" link to node `40000938-5082` in the Design System 2026 file.
- That exact same node (`40000938-5082`) is referenced in SFCC-736's own comment thread and is the frame `zimmDrawer.css.ts` was already measured against (see its "Large = 50%... Small = 25%" comment) — i.e., the shell-level sizing design already has a Figma source *and* a shipped implementation.
- SFCC-315 was explicitly approved by Emma Kirwan on 2026-09-01 — three weeks after the tracker's last check (2026-08-10) — with only copy/config flagged as unconfirmed.

I did not open the Figma files or images myself (no visual verification), so I can't confirm completeness beyond what the ticket metadata shows. But the tracker's "Incomplete" status and this ticket's own approved, image-and-link-backed state don't agree — this reads like the same kind of tracker/reality drift already logged elsewhere for this project (Figma sign-off status), not a settled "no design exists."

### Shared drawer-shell cross-story flag + reusability checks

**Cross-story flag confirmed and strengthened.** SFCC-315, SFCC-801 (currency selector, Blocked), and SFCC-831 (language mismatch) all depend on the same generic shell concept per the given ground truth. I found a fourth: **SFCC-847 "drawer/content/filters"** (In Refinement) also formally `relates to` SFCC-736 in Jira — a filter drawer, presumably PLP-side, not previously named. Worth treating as a fourth consumer of the same "build once" question, not a separate blocker.

**SFCC-736 reusability check — the shell is genuinely generic, not PDP-specific plumbing.** Verified directly in code, not inferred from the ticket text:
